summary: WebSocket subprotocol inconsistency yields duplicated-leading-tokens and truncated-sentences on reconnect
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports repeated occurrences where a websocket streaming session that undergoes a short disconnect and then reconnect emits duplicate leading tokens and occasionally drops the final sentence. The duplicated tokens are identical prefixes that appear immediately after reconnect, and in several cases the client receives a truncated final sentence mid-word.

Impact:
- Affects small subset of requests to AuroraForms' dedicated pool in eu-west-1; observed on ~0.4% of streaming sessions for that pool over last 48h.
- Produces corrupted user-visible paragraphs for customers using client-side stitching, leading to application-level retries and content duplication.

Environment:
- Dedicated deployment (customer-dedicated GPU pool) in eu-west-1
- Model: redwood-v2-large pinned to v2026-02-14
- Client: AuroraForms iOS app using websocket streaming with custom subprotocol header 'rw-stream-v1'
- Edge: traffic flows through our edge-router -> ws-proxy -> serving-runtime chain; TLS terminated at edge-router

Steps to reproduce (as reported by customer):
1. Start websocket stream from iOS app with subprotocol 'rw-stream-v1' and application-level keepalive=20s.
2. Trigger a short network transition (Wi-Fi -> cellular) causing a transient TCP reset and a reconnect within 2-6s.
3. After reconnect client resumes with same session-id and sends resume offset header.
4. Client observes duplicated prefix tokens and on ~1/10 reproductions the last sentence is cut mid-word.

Observed behavior:
- Duplicate sequence of tokens exactly matching the last 8-12 tokens before the disconnect (e.g., "...the quick brown fox\n\n...the quick brown fox") appears immediately after the resume.
- In 10-12% of reproduced cases the stream ends without an end-of-stream marker and the final sentence truncates on a UTF-8 boundary.
- Server-side logs show a short sequence of back-to-back session handoffs with different upstream connection ids.

Expected behavior:
- Resume should stitch on resume-offset without replaying already-delivered tokens and should always produce properly terminated UTF-8 payloads.

Attachments/Logs:
- Customer provided client pcap and app logs (attached to ticket).
- Server trace id examples: trace-eu-7721-0a6f, trace-eu-7721-0b9a, trace-eu-7721-0c1e.
- Edge-router and ws-proxy logs attached in internal log bundle: s3://redwood-logs/sup-123456/log-bundle.zip

Temporary workaround suggested to customer:
- Toggle client to use explicit 'resume=false' on reconnect and re-open a new stream (avoids duplication but increases tokens consumed).
comments: 2026-03-01 09:12 - Support (Ava Martinez): Customer reports that duplication begins after brief mobile network flaps. Asked for pcaps and exact client headers. Customer uploaded pcap and example session ids.

2026-03-01 11:05 - SRE (Nora Patel): Initial tail of ws-proxy logs shows two different upstream socket ids for a single session-id within 200ms; looks like a mid-handshake swap at the proxy. Pulling matching router logs.

2026-03-01 14:30 - Eng (Liam O'Connor): Reproduced locally using a test harness that simulates subprotocol negotiation + quick socket teardown. Observed duplicated leading tokens when ws-proxy advertises subprotocol mismatch during reconnect handshake. Opened PR #829 to add stricter subprotocol validation and a resumeid check.

2026-03-02 08:20 - Customer (AuroraForms - Mateo Ruiz): Confirmed switching to resume=false eliminates duplicated prefixes in our app. Would prefer a server-side fix so we can keep resume for UX reasons.
2026-03-03 10:02 - Eng (Liam O'Connor): Patch candidate merged into canary (serving-runtime PR 829). Monitoring canary in eu-west-1 for 24h; will roll forward if error rate drops.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis A: During reconnect the ws-proxy sometimes returns an upgraded connection with different subprotocol negotiation state; the client resumes using old resume-offset while proxy maps to a fresh upstream connection, causing duplicate token emission.

Hypothesis B: Keepalive coalescing at edge-router can swallow or reorder small finish markers under TCP fast-retransmit leading to missing EoS control frame. UTF-8 cut observed correlates with 2-4ms bursts in the pcap around closure.

Findings:
- Trace analysis shows session-id persisted but upstream-connection-id changed.
- Canary with stricter subprotocol enforcement (PR 829) reduced duplicate prefix incidents from 0.4% to 0.01% in eu-west-1 canary subset.
- UTF-8 truncation cases appear when resume handshake completes but the trailing EoS control frame is not observed by ws-proxy due to a narrow race with connection close; this is rarer and may need an additional guard (idempotent EoS ack).
resolution_notes:
Canary patch merged and promoted to staging. Mitigations: (1) ws-proxy now verifies subprotocol on resume and rejects reconnects where the negotiated subprotocol diverges from session metadata; (2) added idempotent end-of-stream ack and a 150ms guard window before treating upstream connection as closed to reduce rare UTF-8 truncation race.
Rollout plan: 24h canary in eu-west-1 -> 48h progressive rollout to dedicated fleets. Customer notified and will validate; recommended client fallback of resume=false as interim.
Related PR: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/829
Follow-ups: Add longer-term test harness for mid-handshake socket swap scenarios and a unit test for resume offset idempotency.
resolution: Partial fix deployed to canary and staging; monitoring ongoing. Customer workaround documented.
next_steps: Continue monitoring eu-west-1 canary for 72 hours and collect duplicate-token metrics.
Create automated fuzz tests for websocket subprotocol negotiation races (owner: Eng/Streaming).
